59938435.s: Al Baha Museum, one of the museums of Al Baha Region, was founded in 1424 AH. It displays pieces, fossils and old tools from the Stone Age and from eras more than 3,500 years before the Common Era, along with many artefacts from the Mousterian period. A copy of the Holy Quran, dated 1280 AH and presented to the museum by Prince Nayef bin Abdulaziz, is a highlight. The museum began in a rented building until the Antiquities and Museums Agency built a permanent home for it, choosing Raghdan Forest as a suitable site.

59938432.s: Al Malad Castle is one of the most important historic landmarks in the village. It consists of two neighbouring forts built long ago by two brothers for military observation and used by them as food stores. Beside the two towers stands a building where peace agreements between tribes were concluded and commercial deals were made in the past. They lie on the old trade route leading south to Asir.

59938430.s: Thee Ain is an archaeological village in Tihamah, western Saudi Arabia, about 20 kilometres from Al Makhwah Governorate and 24 kilometres from Al Baha. It dates from the tenth century AH and is more than 400 years old. The village is built on top of a white mountain and is known for growing bananas, lemons, peppers, basil and kadi, and for its handicrafts. It has many houses of two to four storeys, a small mosque, and many forts used to defend and watch over the village.

It is also one of ten sites approved by the Saudi government in November 2014 to be put forward to UNESCO for inclusion on the World Heritage List in the coming years.

59938382.s: Al Farsha Park in Qilwah Governorate lies below the summit of Shada Al Ala Mountain. It suits families and young people alike and offers all service facilities, as well as private seating for families, children's amusement rides, a walkway, and various events held in spring.

59938380.s: Shada Al Ala is a high rocky mountain, the highest in the Tihamah plain, lying roughly between the towns of Qilwah and Al Makhwah in south-western Saudi Arabia. Its summit is estimated at 2,200 metres above sea level. The terrain is dominated by smooth rock, giving the mountain a pale blue colour. On the mountain there is an emirate building, a school and a health centre, and electricity is available. A fairly good paved road reaches it, branching off the Al Makhwah-Qilwah road.
59938380.b: Shada Al Ala is a high rocky mountain, the highest in the Tihamah plain, lying roughly between the towns of Qilwah and Al Makhwah in south-western Saudi Arabia. On the mountain there is an emirate building, a school and a health centre, and electricity is available. A fairly good paved road reaches it, branching off the Al Makhwah-Qilwah road. In 2001 Shada Al Ala joined the Kingdom's list of nature reserves because it is home to a number of rare creatures and migratory birds, the most famous of which is the Arabian leopard.
59938380.a: Shada Al Ala Mountain, Shada, Al Makhwah

59938335.s: The Tuesday Market in Al Makhwah is one of the largest traditional markets in Al Baha Region. It lies east of Al Makhwah, near the road leading to the city of Al Baha. Vendors, most of them from Tihamah, sell dates, honey, vegetables, fruit and grain throughout the week. On Tuesdays part of the market is set aside for selling livestock, birds and farming tools, alongside clothing, perfumes and heritage items.

59938312.s: Wadi Al Ahsabah is one of the longest valleys in southern Saudi Arabia. It lies in Tihamah and runs from east to west, flowing into the Red Sea. It is 50 km long, with several tributaries flowing into it, the most important of which are Batat and Shada, and it passes through many towns.
